name: The early boats
words: A free video whose player travels between its screen in the world and a corner of the phone's screen.

captions.text: Every morning the boats leave before the sun.
The first light comes up behind the headland.
The lamp on the point still turns.
Listen: the gulls know where the boats are going.
By the time the sky is blue, the nets are out.
The water is calm this close to the shore.
In the afternoon they come back, low in the water.
And the harbour fills with voices again.

longest.title: The early boats, the late boats and the long argument over the harbour lamp

captions.text: Every morning, long before the sun is up, the boats leave the harbour one after the other.
The first light comes up behind the headland, and the lamp on the point keeps turning until it is full day.
For many years the boat masters argued about who should pay for the oil that kept that lamp burning.
By the time the sky is blue, the nets are out, and the gulls follow the boats far beyond the point.
In the afternoon they come back low in the water, and the harbour fills with voices again.
Some say the lamp is lit only for the boats that are late; others say it is lit for everyone.
The mill turns when the wind comes from the sea.
Its sails were mended every spring.
The miller lived on the first floor.
Flour dust lay on everything, even the cat.
In the evening the sails were locked in a cross.
And the mill waited for the next wind.
